exceptions.severity: high (CVSS 7.5), unchanged. Not fixed: no patched picomatch exists
exceptions.scope: Development, test and build tooling only. Absent from the production dependency tree (npm audit --omit=dev: 0 findings; npm ls --omit=dev: no picomatch), from apps/api/dist and apps/web/dist, and therefore from the Windows package, which ships only those builds
exceptions.reason: The advisory covers every picomatch release up to 4.0.7 (the latest) and lists no patched version; npm's only offered fixes downgrade vitest to 3 and vite to 6 (breaking) and still leave the typescript-eslint path. Exploitation needs an attacker-chosen glob pattern. Only repository-authored patterns reach picomatch: Vite's built-in fs.deny list (not overridden), vitest include/exclude, tsconfig include and ESLint files; request paths are matched against those fixed patterns, never compiled as patterns. The Vite dev server binds to 127.0.0.1 only. Measured 2026-11-18: fixed patterns under 1 ms on 50,000-character hostile inputs; the advisory pattern +(*a) grows from 19 ms to 242 ms between 20 and 26 characters
exceptions.remediation: Check the advisory (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf) and picomatch releases daily. When a fixed picomatch is published and is at least 14 days old (package-age policy), update it together with any of vite, vitest, tinyglobby or typescript-eslint that need it, confirm npm audit no longer reports GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf, and delete this entry. If no fix can be applied by 2026-11-25, the gate fails until the owner explicitly reviews and renews this entry
